extraction.name: EgoLife
extraction.description: A comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset with intensive annotation, collected from six participants living together for one week to prepare an Earth Day celebration, with synchronized third-person video and multimodal signals.
extraction.creator: The EgoLife Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected over a seven-day period with six volunteers residing in a custom-designed environment called the EgoHouse. Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses and captured multimodal egocentric videos for approximately eight hours daily. To enhance the dataset with third-person perspectives, 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded activities from multiple angles. Additionally, millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data, supporting synchronized multimodal analysis. Participants were asked to organize an Earth Day party on the second-to-last day, and activities included discussions, shopping, cooking, socializing, entertainment, rehearsals, decorating, sightseeing, and outings. Recording permission was obtained in locations like shopping malls. The project also includes a Milan session collected in a different environment.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data includes first-person video from 6 Aria glasses, third-person video from fixed indoor cameras, synchronized multimodal signal data including millimeter-wave radars and WiFi signals, as well as audio, IMU, and gaze data. File formats listed include MP4 for video+audio, CSV for IMU, gaze, and radar signal data, HDF5 for WiFi signal data, and JSON for annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Beijing: seven days; Milan: one day
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Videos, audio, IMU, and GoPro data were synchronized using the EgoSync codebase. The pipeline included privacy protection through EgoBlur, dense captioning through EgoCaption, and transcription through EgoTranscript. For transcript creation, synchronized egocentric videos had audio tracks from six participants merged into one, speech recognition applied, diarization used to differentiate speakers, then audio was split back into six participant-specific tracks and reviewed. For captions, initial short narrations were merged into coherent sentences using GPT-4o-mini and then expanded into visual-audio captions by pairing with representative frames sampled at 1 FPS and corresponding transcripts, summarized by GPT-4o.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rigorous data cleaning process was implemented to ensure synchronization, participant privacy, and readiness for annotation and release. Data preprocessing included multimodal signal extraction and alignment with video data, multi-view synchronization using timestamps, de-identification by blurring all participant faces, bystanders' faces, vehicle license plates, and sensitive screen content, and muting sensitive audio segments. Audio was also processed to enhance clarity for Q&A annotations. Due to storage limitations, recordings were structured into three-hour segments, with periodic collection for upload and storage clearance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcript annotation began after synchronizing egocentric videos, merging audio tracks from six participants, and applying speech recognition to generate initial timestamped transcripts. An open-source diarization algorithm differentiated speakers, and reviewers refined the transcripts to keep only speech audible to each participant. For caption annotations, videos were split into 5-minute clips and slowed to 0.8x speed. Annotators provided continuous detailed narrations by speaking without pauses, covering actions, interactions, and environmental details. Narration was converted to text via a transcription tool, then reviewed and corrected for synchronized, time-aligned descriptions. Initial narrations of 361K brief phrases were merged into 25K coherent captions using GPT-4o-mini, then expanded into visual-audio captions using representative frames sampled at 1 FPS, transcripts, and GPT-4o, followed by human verification. For EgoLifeQA, five question types were designed: EntityLog, EventRecall, HabitInsight, RelationMap, and TaskMaster. Visual-audio captions were fed into GPT-4o in batches to generate around 100K timestamped questions per participant. These AI-generated questions were provided to annotators as SRT files for filtering and inspiration. Only questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior were retained, then rigorously selected and refined down to 500 QA per participant. Annotators also generated distractors for multiple-choice questions and annotated whether audio was required and the look-back time needed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The preliminary 50-hour merged transcript with overlapping conversations was reviewed for accuracy, then refined into participant-specific audible speech transcripts. For captions, narration text was reviewed and corrected for synchronization and time alignment. Initial subtitle-like narrations were merged into coherent sentences and expanded into visual-audio captions, which were verified by human annotators. For QA annotation, around 100K AI-generated questions per participant were filtered to 1K high-quality questions and then further curated to 500 QA per participant. Annotators also labeled whether audio was required to answer each question and specified the certification length necessary for retrieving the correct answer.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Reviewers, annotators, and one of the five external volunteers during the EgoLife casting week are mentioned, but no demographic details are provided.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Whisper Large v3; open-source diarization algorithm; GPT-4o-mini; GPT-4o
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The project is described as ongoing. The Beijing dataset has been fully annotated and synchronized, while the Milan dataset has been collected and will be detailed in an upcoming EgoLife blog series. The authors state that the annotation partnership will continue for future EgoLife versions and that they plan to expand the dataset to cover a broader range of languages, locations, and activities.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Faces, bystanders' faces, vehicle license plates, mobile or computer screen content such as passwords or personal data, private or potentially identifiable audio information, spoken language, participant identities, and person-specific daily habits and social interactions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that EgoButler and the EgoLifeQA dataset hold significant potential to enhance human-AI interaction, particularly in personalized assistance and context-aware applications. It suggests benefits for daily activities, personal organization, contextual reminders, education, professional settings, the elderly, and individuals with cognitive challenges. It also emphasizes the need to address privacy and ethical considerations, user autonomy, trust, data privacy safeguards, and transparency in AI decision-making to ensure positive societal reception.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The work intentionally started with a narrow setting, sacrificing some generalizability, such as single language and scenario. The primary language of the dataset is Chinese, though a one-day predominantly English session was also conducted. The authors also note model overfitting to early observations in personalization, such as misidentifying people based on clothing seen on Day-1.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes limitations in current models and dataset scope. It intentionally starts with a narrow setting with limited generalizability, including a single main language and scenario. Due to storage limitations, recordings were structured into three-hour segments with interruptions for upload and storage clearance. The authors note that EgoGPT's speech understanding remains incomplete, it struggles with laughter and emotions, identity recognition can overfit to early observations, and EgoRAG lacks multi-step reasoning and error tolerance. The dataset currently covers Beijing fully and Milan only as a collected but not yet detailed subset.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to support development of multimodal egocentric AI assistants, long-context life-oriented question answering, human behavior recognition, multimodal signal analysis, human-machine interaction, long-duration activity understanding, interpersonal dynamics, contextual interactions, synchronized human behavior analysis, ego-exo alignment, and training EgoGPT. Visual-audio captions serve two main purposes: training EgoGPT and automatically generating QA candidates. EgoLifeQA is used as a benchmark for multiple-choice question answering and evaluation of long-term life assistant capabilities.
